explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/818: for a finite set A of integers with |A+A| ≪ |A|, is |AA| ≫ |A|²/(log|A|)^C for some constant C > 0? Proved by Solymosi. The Lean statement unpacks the two Vinogradov symbols correctly: ∀ K > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∃ c > 0, ∀ finite A ⊂ ℤ with |A| ≥ 2 and |A+A| ≤ K|A|, c·|A|²/(log|A|)^C ≤ |A·A|. The constants C and c are allowed to depend on the doubling constant K, and |A| ≥ 2 keeps log|A| positive. Faithful.
